ky_coyote_cliff.blurb: Coyote Cliff is a quiet wall tucked into Muir Valley, a sandstone preserve in the Red River Gorge near Rogers. About twenty routes, mostly bolted with a couple of trad lines and two top-ropes, run from an easy 5.4 up past 5.13, though the bulk sit between 5.10 and 5.12. The stone is often smooth slab or water-polished grooves, so expect technical, balancy climbing rather than big jugs, and some lines can be dirty. The wall faces northwest and stays mostly shaded, with a mossy fern garden at its base. It sees far fewer people than the headline walls in the valley, and the short walk in makes it an easy add-on.

ky_bibliothek.blurb: Bibliothek is a steep sport wall in Muir Valley, in the Red River Gorge near Rogers, Kentucky. Nearly all of the roughly twenty routes are bolted, with two trad lines mixed in. Most fall in the 5.11 range, with a handful of 5.12s and just a few easier or harder outliers, so it suits climbers who already lead 5.10 and want volume. Expect overhanging sandstone and sustained, pumpy 65 to 70 foot pitches, which makes it a good place to build endurance for steeper 5.12s. The wall picks up shade in the afternoon, which helps on warm days. The approach is a longer walk than at the valley's roadside walls.

ky_hideout_the.blurb: The Hideout is a lightly visited wall in Muir Valley, a sandstone preserve in the Red River Gorge near Rogers. Its twenty routes split almost evenly between bolted lines and gear climbs, spanning about 5.7 to 5.12, with the largest cluster in the 5.10 range and a good number of easier 5.7 to 5.9 options too. The climbing leans technical, a change of pace from the jug hauls found on nearby walls. The base is usually shady, and the cliff is a poor choice in wet weather. Because it draws few people, you can often have it to yourself, and the hike up the hill from the valley road is short.

ky_dip_wall.blurb: Dip Wall is a trad-focused cliff in the Northern Gorge of the Red River Gorge, set in Daniel Boone National Forest in a pretty wooded hollow. All twenty routes here are protected by gear, ranging from a 5.3 up to the low 5.12 range, and the majority sit between 5.7 and 5.10. The cliff is tall, yet most of the lines are short, and many run beneath big blank overhangs, which keeps them dry in the rain; that makes it a favourite wet-day trad stop. It faces mostly south, so it warms nicely in winter. A few easier bolted lines also suit newer leaders. The approach follows a creek, an old road and a switchback.

ky_lower_small_wall.blurb: Lower Small Wall is the biggest of the three Small Walls in the Northern Gorge of the Red River Gorge, in Daniel Boone National Forest. It is a mixed bag of about twenty problems and routes: mostly trad lines from an easy 5.2 or so up to around 5.11, plus a handful of boulder problems from V0 to V3 that sit close to the road, apart from the main cliff. The wall faces south, so it gets plenty of sun. The hike up from a roadside pull-off is steep but short. It has a reputation for adventure and a bit of mystery, and suits climbers who like exploring more than clipping bolts.
